header.userPrompt:
Implement GitHub issue softwaremill/ox#528: "Flow.fromPublisher: allow releasing elements which are buffered but not emitted".

Problem: `Flow.fromPublisher` (core/src/main/scala/ox/flow/FlowCompanionReactiveOps.scala) buffers elements in a channel. Some of them never reach the consumer:
- when the publisher fails, `channel.error` drops the buffered elements
- when the consumer stops early (an exception, an interruption), the buffered elements are never received
- elements can still arrive (onNext) after the subscription is cancelled

If elements hold resources (e.g. Netty's reference-counted ByteBufs), nobody releases them, so they leak.

Goal: add an optional callback, e.g. `fromPublisher(p, onDiscard: T => Unit)`, called exactly once for each element received from the publisher but not emitted downstream. Existing call sites without the callback must keep compiling and behaving the same.

Suggested implementation: on publisher error, store the error and call `channel.done()` (so buffered elements are kept and emitted before the error is rethrown). When the flow ends early, cancel the subscription, close the channel, and drain it, calling the callback for each drained element. In `onNext`, call the callback if the channel is already closed. Make sure there are no races where an element is neither emitted nor discarded.

Also update the variant in flow-reactive-streams/src/main/scala/ox/flow/reactive/flowReactiveStreamsExtension.scala (org.reactivestreams Publisher) to accept the same optional callback, and update any docs (doc/ directory) describing fromPublisher.

Acceptance criteria:
- tests covering: publisher error with buffered elements (elements still emitted, then error); consumer stopping early (exception / interruption) with buffered elements -> callback called for each; elements arriving after cancellation -> callback called; every element is either emitted or discarded, never both or neither.
- `sbt compile test` passes for affected modules (core, flow-reactive-streams).
- Code follows existing style in the repo; concise doc comments.

Context: tapir currently tracks unconsumed elements itself using a lock: https://github.com/softwaremill/tapir/pull/5573

resultJson.description:
`Flow.fromPublisher` buffers elements received from a reactive `Publisher` in a channel. Today, elements that are buffered but never emitted are silently lost: `channel.error` drops the buffer on publisher error, a consumer that stops early (exception, interruption, `take`) never receives what is buffered, and `onNext` calls that arrive after the subscription is cancelled are dropped by `channel.send` throwing. When elements own resources (Netty reference-counted ByteBufs in tapir), this leaks them. Tapir currently works around it with its own lock-based tracking (softwaremill/tapir#5573).

This epic adds an optional `onDiscard: T => Unit` callback to `Flow.fromPublisher` (core, JDK `Flow.Publisher`) and `FlowReactiveStreams.fromPublisher` (flow-reactive-streams, `org.reactivestreams.Publisher`), with the invariant that every element received from the publisher is either emitted downstream or passed to `onDiscard`, exactly once, never both or neither. Publisher errors no longer drop buffered elements: the error is stored, the channel is completed with `done()`, buffered elements are emitted, and then the error is rethrown. When the flow ends early, the subscription is cancelled, the channel is closed and drained through `onDiscard`, and any late `onNext` goes to `onDiscard` as well. Existing single-argument call sites keep compiling (the new parameter is an overload, which also keeps MiMa happy for `core`). Docs in `doc/streaming/flows.md` describe the new callback.

tasks.title: Add onDiscard overload to Flow.fromPublisher in core, with tests for error, early stop and late onNext
tasks.description:
In core/src/main/scala/ox/flow/FlowCompanionReactiveOps.scala add `def fromPublisher[T](p: Publisher[T], onDiscard: T => Unit)(using BufferCapacity): Flow[T]` and make the existing one-arg `fromPublisher` delegate to it with `_ => ()`. Implement per the brief's design decisions: `onNext` uses `sendOrClosed` and discards on closed; `onError` stores the throwable in an AtomicReference and calls `doneOrClosed`; `onComplete` calls `doneOrClosed`; `onSubscribe` cancels immediately if a `cancelled` flag is already set, else requests `capacity`; the consumer loop rethrows the stored error when it sees `Done`; on any Throwable escaping the loop: set `cancelled`, cancel the subscription if present, `doneOrClosed` the channel, drain it calling `onDiscard` per element (keep draining across an InterruptedException and re-interrupt the thread afterwards), rethrow. Preserve the existing batched demand logic. Update the scaladoc of both overloads (exactly-once invariant, callback runs on publisher threads and must not throw, buffered elements are now emitted before a publisher error is rethrown).

Tests, in a new core/src/test/scala/ox/flow/reactive/FlowFromPublisherDiscardTest.scala (AnyFunSuite with Matchers), using a hand-written `ManualPublisher[T]` helper as described in the brief (keep the helper in this file or a sibling file in the same package so Task 2 can reuse it):
1. Publisher error with buffered elements: push 1,2,3 then `error(boom)` before/while the consumer runs; `runToList` throws boom and all of 1,2,3 were emitted; `onDiscard` never called.
2. Publisher error with nothing buffered still throws.
3. Consumer exception: `.map(x => if x == 2 then throw boom else x)`, push 1..5; `runToList` throws boom; discarded == 3,4,5 (order-independent compare), subscription cancelled.
4. Consumer stops via `take(2)`: result List(1,2), discarded == 3,4,5, cancelled.
5. Consumer interrupted: run `runForeach(x => { received.release(); gate.acquire() })` in `forkCancellable`, push 1..5, wait for `received`, `cancel()`; discarded == 2,3,4,5, cancelled.
6. Late onNext after cancellation: after any of the above, call `next(6)` on the publisher; `onDiscard(6)` is called synchronously and nothing throws.
7. Existing one-arg overload: compiles unchanged and `FlowPublisherPekkoTest` still passes.
Run `sbt "core/testOnly ox.flow.reactive.*"` and `sbt core/scalafmt`; all green.

tasks.title: Exactly-once stress test: every element is emitted or discarded, never both or neither
tasks.description: Add a test (same file as Task 1 or a sibling in core/src/test/scala/ox/flow/reactive/) that uses a demand-respecting publisher running on its own thread: it emits 1..N (N around 1000) only while `sent < requested` and not cancelled, calling `onNext` from that thread, then `onComplete`. Compose `Flow.fromPublisher(p, discarded.add)` with a consumer that stops at a random point (e.g. `take(k)` for random k, and separately a `map` that throws at a random element, and separately a `forkCancellable` cancelled after a random short delay). Collect emitted elements via `.tap(emitted.add)` into thread-safe collections. After the flow finishes and the publisher thread is joined, assert: `emitted` and `discarded` are disjoint, their union equals exactly the set of elements the publisher actually sent, and no element appears twice. Repeat each scenario in a loop (e.g. 20 iterations) with a small `given BufferCapacity = BufferCapacity(4)` to make buffer-full races likely. The publisher's late `onNext` calls (after cancellation) must land in `discarded`. If this exposes a race in Task 1's implementation, fix it in FlowCompanionReactiveOps.scala as part of this task. Run `sbt "core/testOnly ox.flow.reactive.*"`.

tasks.description: In doc/streaming/flows.md, section "### Publisher -> Flow" (around lines 211-219), add a short paragraph explaining: elements received from the publisher but not emitted downstream (buffered when the publisher fails, when the consumer stops early via exception, interruption or `take`, or arriving after cancellation) can be released by passing a second argument `onDiscard: T => Unit` to `Flow.fromPublisher` / `FlowReactiveStreams.fromPublisher`; it is called exactly once per such element, possibly from the publisher's thread, and should not throw; typical use is releasing reference-counted buffers. resultJson.brief:
## Modules and files

- `core/src/main/scala/ox/flow/FlowCompanionReactiveOps.scala` — the only implementation file in core. Trait `FlowCompanionReactiveOps` (mixed into `Flow.type`) defines `def fromPublisher[T](p: java.util.concurrent.Flow.Publisher[T])(using BufferCapacity): Flow[T]`. Read the whole file (80 lines) before changing anything. Current structure: `usingEmitInline: emit => unsupervised { channel = BufferCapacity.newChannel[T]; forkUnsupervised { p.subscribe(Subscriber: onSubscribe -> subscriptionRef.set(s); s.request(capacity); onNext -> channel.send; onError -> channel.error; onComplete -> channel.done) }; repeatWhile { channel.receiveOrClosed() match Done -> false / Error -> throw / t -> emit(t); batched subscription.request } }.tapException(cancel subscription)`. The demand logic (`demandThreshold = ceil(capacity/2)`, `toDemand` counter, lazily cached `subscription` read from `subscriptionRef` after the first element) must be preserved.
- `flow-reactive-streams/src/main/scala/ox/flow/reactive/flowReactiveStreamsExtension.scala` — `object FlowReactiveStreams { def fromPublisher[T](p: org.reactivestreams.Publisher[T])(using BufferCapacity): Flow[T] = Flow.fromPublisher(FlowAdapters.toFlowPublisher(p)) }`. Module has no `src/test` dir yet; scalatest is already a test dependency (build.sbt `flowReactiveStreams`), it `dependsOn(core)` (compile only, not test->test).
- `core/src/test/scala/ox/flow/reactive/` — existing reactive tests: `FlowPublisherPekkoTest.scala` (AnyFunSuite + Matchers, uses Pekko `Source...runWith(Sink.asPublisher)` and `FlowAdapters.toFlowPublisher`) and `FlowPublisherTckTest.scala`. Put new fromPublisher tests here. No test anywhere currently uses a hand-written Publisher; write one (see below).
- `doc/streaming/flows.md` lines 211-219, section "### Publisher -> Flow" — the only user doc mentioning `fromPublisher`. `generated-doc/out/**` is mdoc output regenerated at release time by `updateDocs`; do NOT edit it. Code blocks in docs use ```` ```scala mdoc:compile-only ```` and are compiled by `sbt compileDocumentation` (slow; only needed if you add a code block). Doc dependency snippet convention: `// sbt dependency: "com.softwaremill.ox" %% "flow-reactive-streams" % "@VERSION@"`.

## Key APIs (ox.channels, core/src/main/scala/ox/channels/Channel.scala)

- `Sink.sendOrClosed(t): Unit | ChannelClosed` (non-throwing), `Sink.send(t)` throws `ChannelClosedException` when closed.
- `Sink.doneOrClosed(): Unit | ChannelClosed` — "buffered values will be delivered; send operations in progress complete normally when a receiver arrives"; returns `ChannelClosed` instead of throwing if already closed. `Sink.errorOrClosed(reason)` — drops buffered values (that is the bug). Use the `*OrClosed` variants everywhere in the subscriber: a misbehaving publisher may call onError/onComplete twice.
- `Source.receiveOrClosed(): T | ChannelClosed` (blocking); match `case ChannelClosed.Done => ...; case e: ChannelClosed.Error => throw e.toThrowable; case t: T @unchecked => ...`. `Source.tryReceiveOrClosed()` is non-blocking but may spuriously return None, so it is not suitable for a drain loop.
- `Source.foreachOrError(f)` / `drainOrError()` from `SourceDrainOps.scala` loop until Done; usable for the drain, but write the drain inline so you can handle `InterruptedException` (see below).
- jox semantics (com.softwaremill.jox channels 1.1.2, verified from source): after `done()`, buffered elements stay receivable; a receiver observing Done has already seen every element whose `send` started before `done()` (an in-progress sender is waited for); a `send` racing with `done()` either lands in the buffer or returns closed. Hence "drain until Done, then `sendOrClosed` returns closed" gives exactly-once discard with no extra locking.
- `BufferCapacity`: `given default: BufferCapacity = 16`; `BufferCapacity.newChannel[T]`; `summon[BufferCapacity].toInt` (import `ox.channels.toInt`). Tests can override with `given BufferCapacity = BufferCapacity(4)`.
- `ox.util`: `t.tapException(f)` runs `f(e)` for any Throwable and rethrows `e` (exceptions from `f` added as suppressed). `ox.pipe`, `ox.discard`, `ox.repeatWhile` already imported in the file.
- `FlowOps.take(n)` stops upstream by throwing a private `ControlThrowable` (`abortTake`) out of `emit`, caught in `take` itself. So "consumer stops early" includes `take`, and the cleanup path must run for every Throwable, not just NonFatal. `tapException`/`catch case e: Throwable` already does this.
- `unsupervised { ... }` + `forkUnsupervised { ... }` (import `ox.unsupervised`, `ox.forkUnsupervised`): scope end interrupts still-running forks once. `onNext`/`onError`/`onComplete` run on the publisher's threads (or on the `p.subscribe` fork for synchronous publishers), never on the consumer thread.
- Test helpers: `ox.forkCancellable { ... }` inside `supervised` returns a `CancellableFork` with `cancel(): Either[Throwable, T]` (interrupts once, joins). Interruption inside the flow surfaces as `InterruptedException` thrown from a blocking call (e.g. `Semaphore.acquire`, `channel.receiveOrClosed`).

## Design decisions (apply as-is)

- API: add an overload `def fromPublisher[T](p: Publisher[T], onDiscard: T => Unit)(using BufferCapacity): Flow[T]` and make the existing one-arg method delegate with `_ => ()`. Do not add a default parameter and do not change the existing signature: `core` runs MiMa (`enableMimaSettings` in build.sbt) and only additive changes are safe. Same shape in `FlowReactiveStreams`.
- Subscriber: `onNext(t)` = `channel.sendOrClosed(t)` and if the result is `ChannelClosed` call `onDiscard(t)`. `onError(e)` = store `e` in an `AtomicReference[Throwable]`, then `channel.doneOrClosed().discard`. `onComplete()` = `channel.doneOrClosed().discard`. `onSubscribe(s)` = set `subscriptionRef`, then if a `cancelled: AtomicBoolean` is already set call `s.cancel()` else `s.request(capacity)` (both sides use volatile atomics, so at least one side sees the other; a double `cancel()` is allowed by the spec).
- Consumer loop: on `ChannelClosed.Done`, read the stored error; if non-null throw it, else finish. Keep the `ChannelClosed.Error` branch for safety.
- Cleanup, run on any Throwable escaping the loop (the stored publisher error included; cancel after onError is a spec-allowed no-op): set `cancelled`, cancel the subscription if `subscriptionRef` is non-null, `channel.doneOrClosed().discard`, then drain: loop `receiveOrClosed()` until `Done`, calling `onDiscard` for each element. The drain is bounded (channel is done, at most capacity elements plus in-flight sends) but blocking; if `InterruptedException` is thrown mid-drain, catch it, keep draining, and call `Thread.currentThread().interrupt()` once the drain finishes, so no element is lost on a second interrupt. Then rethrow the original exception. An element that was passed to `emit` and whose `emit` threw counts as emitted (downstream owns it): do not discard it.
- Scaladoc on the new overload: state the exactly-once invariant, that `onDiscard` may be called from publisher threads, that it must not throw, and that on publisher error buffered elements are emitted before the error is rethrown (this is a deliberate behaviour change for the one-arg variant too; mention it in its doc).

## Test publisher helper (write it in the core test, package `ox.flow.reactive`)

A `ManualPublisher[T] extends java.util.concurrent.Flow.Publisher[T]` with: `@volatile var subscriber: Subscriber[? >: T]`, `requested: AtomicLong`, `cancelled: AtomicBoolean`, a `subscribed: CountDownLatch(1)`; `subscribe(s)` stores `s`, calls `s.onSubscribe(new Subscription { request(n) => requested.addAndGet(n); cancel() => cancelled.set(true) })`, counts down the latch. Helper methods `next(t)`, `error(e)`, `complete()` forward to the subscriber from the test thread. For the exactly-once stress test, a second variant that runs its own thread emitting `1..n` while `sent < requested` and not cancelled. Run the flow under test in `supervised { forkCancellable { ... } }` or `fork`, await `subscribed`, then drive the publisher. Collect emitted elements with `.tap(emitted += _)` or `runForeach`, discarded with `onDiscard = discarded += _` (use thread-safe collections such as `ConcurrentLinkedQueue` or `java.util.Collections.synchronizedList`, since `onDiscard` runs on other threads).

## Conventions / build

- Scala 3 indentation syntax, `end X` markers on long definitions, `.discard` on ignored results (compiler warns otherwise), scalafmt configured in `.scalafmt.conf` (140-column lines); run `sbt core/scalafmt flowReactiveStreams/scalafmt` after editing.
- Comments: short, explain non-obvious reasoning only; never restate code. Scaladoc describes usage and invariants, not implementation.
- Tests: scalatest 3.2.20; the reactive tests use `AnyFunSuite with Matchers` with `test("...")` blocks and Scala 3 colon syntax. `core` runs tests forked (`Test / fork := true`).
- Commands (sbt 2.0.10): `sbt "core/testOnly ox.flow.reactive.*"`, `sbt flowReactiveStreams/test`, `sbt core/mimaReportBinaryIssues` (only meaningful when a previous stable version resolves), `sbt compileDocumentation` for mdoc. Never commit; the user commits.
